about: The Magníficat is Mary's canticle from the Gospel according to Saint Luke (Luke 1:46–55), sung at Roman Vespers. This edition preserves the traditional Latin text and its ten numbered biblical verses, followed separately by the Glory Be doxology.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s02.translation: And my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s03.translation: For he has regarded the lowliness of his handmaid: behold, from now on all generations will call me blessed.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s04.translation: For he who is mighty has done great things for me, and holy is his name.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s05.translation: And his mercy is from generation to generation for those who fear him.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s06.translation: He has shown strength with his arm; he has scattered the proud in the thoughts of their hearts.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s07.translation: He has brought the mighty down from their throne and exalted the lowly.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s08.translation: He has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s09.translation: He has helped Israel, his servant, remembering his mercy.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s10.translation: As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed forever.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s11.translation: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

s12.translation: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

w015.explanation: Greek ταπείνωσις confirms that Mary speaks of her low estate, not in praise of a moral achievement of her own.

w026.explanation: “Generations”, not “nations”: all the ages to come will call her blessed.

w045.explanation: The word names those who fear God and toward whom His mercy extends.

w048.explanation: “Fecit poténtiam” means literally that He wrought or showed strength.

w056.explanation: The pronoun refers to the proud: it is the designs of their hearts that are scattered.

w071.explanation: The verb presents God coming to the aid of Israel, His servant.

w073.explanation: Greek παῖς confirms that Israel is called God's servant here, not a boy.

w080.explanation: With “locútus” it forms the single predicate “has spoken”.

w090.explanation: Latin leaves “sit” unspoken: “Glória [sit] Patri” — “glory [be] to the Father”.
